In which country is Royal Society?
Royal Society: United Kingdom. Founded on 28 November 1660, it was granted a royal charter by King Charles II and is the oldest continuously existing scientific academy in the world.
Who is credited with discovering Caelum?
Caelum: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Caelum SEE-ləm is a faint constellation in the southern sky, introduced in the 1750s by Nicolas Louis de Lacaille and counted among the 88 modern constellations.
Who is credited with discovering 243 Ida?
243 Ida: Johann Palisa. 243 Ida is an asteroid in the Koronis family of the asteroid belt.
Who is credited with discovering Gliese 581d?
Gliese 581d: Stéphane Udry. It was the third planet claimed in the system and the fourth (in a 4-planet model) or fifth (in a disproven 5- or 6-planet model) in order from the star.
Who is credited with discovering Chlorofluorocarbon?
Chlorofluorocarbon: Frédéric Swarts. The most common example of a CFC is dichlorodifluoromethane (R-12).
Sometimes called emotional blindness, this neuropsychological condition involves trouble identifying or describing one's own feelings, and appears in about half of autistic people. What is it?
Alexithymia (-), also called emotional blindness, is a neuropsychological phenomenon characterized by difficulties processing or describing one's emotions.
This type of long-term arthritis causes inflammation where the spine meets the pelvis, with lower back pain as its hallmark symptom. What condition is it?
Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a type of arthritis from the disease spectrum of axial spondyloarthritis.
This medical condition, most often caused in the developed world by liver cirrhosis, is the abnormal buildup of fluid within the abdominal cavity — what is it called?
Ascites is the abnormal build-up of fluid in the abdomen.
Their foliage is almost indistinguishable from a cycad's, but flower-like reproductive organs — some likely insect-pollinated — set these common Mesozoic seed plants apart. Which extinct order?
Bennettitales (also known as cycadeoids) is an extinct order of seed plants that first appeared in the Permian period and became extinct in most areas toward the end of the Cretaceous.
This Russian mathematician-turned-oligarch was worth an estimated $3 billion in 1997 after privatizing state assets like Channel One — yet died impoverished and depressed in 2013. Who was he?
Boris Berezovsky (businessman) (23 January 1946 - 23 March 2013), also known as Platon Elenin, was a Russian business oligarch, government official, engineer and mathematician.
This highly soluble white crystalline salt is commonly spread on roads for de-icing and dust control, and its hygroscopic nature lets it pull moisture straight from the air — what compound is it?
Calcium chloride is an inorganic compound, a salt with the chemical formula CaCl2.
Retired from Istanbul Technical University, this geologist holds foreign membership in both the US and Russian National Academies of Sciences. Who is he?
Celâl Şengör (born 24 March 1955) is a Turkish geologist.
This common name covers many species of bivalve mollusc that use a powerful foot to burrow into sand or mud, with two equal shells joined by adductor muscles — what creature is it?
Clam is a common name for several species of bivalve mollusc. In culinary usage, clams are commonly eaten marine bivalves, as in clam digging and the resulting soup, clam chowder.
This fungal plant disease disfigures maize with galls, yet in Mexican cuisine the infected kernels are prized as huitlacoche, a filling for quesadillas and soups — which disease?
Corn smut is a plant disease caused by the pathogenic fungus Mycosarcoma maydis, synonym Ustilago maydis.
In psychiatry, this is a fixed belief that persists even in the face of clear and obvious evidence to the contrary, distinguishing it from a merely mistaken or strongly held idea — what is it called?
Delusion is a fixed belief that is not amenable to change in light of conflicting evidence.
This unexplained skin condition produces itchy, fluid-filled blisters just millimeters wide on the palms, fingers, or soles, often clearing within a month only to recur — what is it?
Dyshidrosis is a type of dermatitis, characterized by itchy vesicles of 1-2 mm in size, on the palms of the hands, sides of fingers, or bottoms of the feet.
This thin, protective tissue type lines the outer surfaces of organs and the inner surfaces of blood vessels; the skin's outermost layer is a familiar example. What is it?
Epithelium is a thin, continuous, protective layer of cells with little extracellular matrix.
This intracellular protein buffers the body against both iron deficiency and iron overload, and small amounts leak into the blood where doctors measure it as a diagnostic marker — what protein is it?
Ferritin is a universal intracellular and extracellular protein that stores iron and releases it in a controlled fashion.
With about 37 species ranging from central Canada down to Costa Rica, this slender, keeled-scaled reptile typically sports longitudinal stripes in blue, yellow, or red — which reptile is it?
Garter snake is the common name for small to medium-sized snakes belonging to the genus Thamnophis in the family Colubridae.

This Russian mathematician resigned his research post in 2005 and later declared he'd quit the field entirely, disillusioned by its ethical standards, and now lives in seclusion in Saint Petersburg — who is he?
Grigori Perelman (born 13 June 1966) is a Russian mathematician and geometer who is known for his contributions to the fields of geometric analysis, Riemannian geometry, and geometric topology.
With a soft, uncalcified abdomen left dangerously exposed, this crustacean borrows empty snail shells to survive — over 800 species haul their homes around with them. What are they?
Hermit crab are anomuran decapod crustaceans of the superfamily Paguroidea that have adapted to occupy empty scavenged gastropod shells to protect their fragile abdomens.
Triggered by causes like vomiting, diarrhea, or the diuretic furosemide, this condition denotes a blood potassium level under 3.5 mmol/L — what is it?
Hypokalemia is a low level of potassium (K+) in the blood serum.
Native to Africa and Eurasia, which group of opportunistic canid predators includes the black-backed, side-striped, and golden species?
Jackal are canids native to Africa and Eurasia.
This occupation and set of methods involves producing and distributing reports on events and people that make up the 'news of the day,' with a commitment to accuracy — what is it?
Journalism is the production and distribution of reports on events, facts, ideas, and people that constitute the "news of the day" and inform society with a commitment to accuracy and verification.
Shaped by constitutions and produced through statutes, regulations or judicial precedent, this body of enforced rules governs behavior and shapes politics and society — what is it?
Law is a set of rules that are created and enforced by governmental or societal institutions to regulate behavior, with its precise definition a matter of longstanding debate.

Built by an American defense contractor with partners including Northrop Grumman and BAE Systems, this single-engine, single-seat stealth fighter comes in conventional, short-takeoff, and carrier-launched variants — name the aircraft?
Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II is an American family of single-seat, single-engine, supersonic stealth strike fighters.
An economist by training, he became the only Sikh to lead India and the first prime minister since Nehru to be re-appointed after a full five-year term — who is he?
Manmohan Singh (26 September 1932 - 26 December 2024) was an Indian economist, bureaucrat, academician and statesman who served as the prime minister of India from 2004 to 2014.
Sold dissolved in solution or shipped anhydrous in pressurized railcars, this simplest primary amine reeks like rotten fish — what compound is it?
Methylamine is an organic compound with a formula of CH5N or CH3NH2.
This Bangladeshi economist pioneered microcredit and founded Grameen Bank, work that earned him the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize before he later led an interim government — who is he?
Muhammad Yunus (born 28 June 1940) is a Bangladeshi economist and statesman.
Born in the Austro-Hungarian Empire and emigrating to the US in 1884, he's known for pioneering the AC electricity system. Who?
Nikola Tesla (10 July 1856 - 7 January 1943) was a Serbian-American engineer, futurist, and inventor.
Also covering the modification of facial growth known as dentofacial orthopedics, this branch of dentistry corrects mal-positioned teeth and bite patterns. What field is it?

Orthodontics (also referred to as orthodontia) is a dentistry specialty that addresses the diagnosis, prevention, management, and correction of mal-positioned teeth and jaws, as well as misaligned bite patterns.
This species of hickory tree, native to the Mississippi River region of the southern US and northern Mexico, is the official state nut of five states and the state tree of Texas. What nut is this?
Pecan (pih-KAN,; Carya illinoinensis) is a species of hickory native to the Southern United States and northern Mexico in the region of the Mississippi River.
These drifting, self-feeding members of the plankton community photosynthesize like land plants, so they crowd the sunlit surface waters of oceans and lakes — what are they?
Phytoplankton are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.
A staple food across the world, this tuber is actually an underground stem from a plant in the nightshade family, with wild relatives growing from the southern U.S. all the way to Chile. What is it?
Potato is a starchy tuberous vegetable native to the Americas that is consumed as a staple food in many parts of the world.
Named partly for the Aztec feathered serpent god and partly for the designer of a tailless aircraft, this genus of giant pterosaur soared over Late Cretaceous North America — what is it?
Quetzalcoatlus is a genus of azhdarchid pterosaur that lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous in North America.
One of the U.S. Air Force's three strategic bombers, this supersonic swing-wing aircraft hauls a 75,000-pound payload and answers to the affectionate name 'Bone' — what is it?
Rockwell B-1 Lancer is a supersonic variable-sweep wing, heavy bomber used by the United States Air Force.

Sitting near the center of the Milky Way between Libra and Sagittarius, this zodiac constellation's recognition predates Greek civilization, and it was among the 48 catalogued by Ptolemy in the second century — what's the constellation?
Scorpius is a zodiac constellation located in the Southern celestial hemisphere, where it sits near the center of the Milky Way, between Libra to the west and Sagittarius to the east.
Marked by reduced muscle activity yet busy, active brain patterns, this state alternates between REM and non-REM cycles — what is it?
Sleep is a state of reduced mental and physical activity in which consciousness is altered and certain sensory activity is inhibited.
An English dyer and astronomer, this man's 1729 experiments were the first to systematically show that electricity could travel through metals and appear on the surface of insulators — who was he?
Stephen Gray (scientist) (December 1666 - February 1736) was an English dyer and astronomer who was the first to systematically experiment with electrical conduction.
Modern practitioners prioritize common ancestry as they sort living things into ranked taxa, from domain and kingdom all the way down to species — which biological discipline does this?

Taxonomy (biology) (from Ancient Greek (taxis) 'arrangement' and - (-nomia) 'method') is the scientific study of naming, defining (circumscribing) and classifying groups of biological organisms based on shared characteristics.
A staple of Mexican cuisine grown as an annual despite being naturally perennial, this small green-purple fruit is best known for flavoring salsa verde — what is it?
Tomatillo (Physalis philadelphica and Physalis ixocarpa), also known as the Mexican husk tomato, is a plant of the nightshade family bearing small, spherical, and green or green-purple fruit.
This medical condition involves involuntary muscle spasms that interfere with vaginal intercourse or other penetration, often causing pain from the first attempt — what is it?
Vaginismus is a condition in which involuntary muscle spasm interferes with vaginal intercourse or other penetration of the vagina.

This genus of four woody, twining vine species in the legume family is native across East Asia and parts of North America, and became a popular ornamental after being introduced to Europe — what genus is it?
Wisteria is a genus of flowering plants in the legume family, Fabaceae (Leguminosae).
This bird-of-prey family boasts 256 species including eagles, hawks, kites, and harriers, though the osprey and secretary bird are classified separately — which family is it?
Accipitridae: Family of birds of prey. The Accipitridae have a cosmopolitan distribution, being found on all the world's continents (except Antarctica) and a number of oceanic island groups.
Conceived as a clean-sheet 'extra wide body' answer to Boeing's Dreamliner, this twin-engine jet first lifted off from Toulouse in 2013 on Rolls-Royce Trent power — which airliner is it?
Airbus A350: Large twin-aisle airliner family.
This American economist shared the 2012 Nobel for the theory of stable allocations and "market design" — applying economic theory to real-world matching problems; who is he?
Consisting of a phenyl group attached to an amino group, this organic compound smells like rotten fish and serves as a key precursor to polyurethane and dyes — what is it called?
Aniline: Organic compound (C6H5NH2); simplest aromatic amine.
Native to the northern tundra, this small mammal grows thick white fur for winter camouflage and forms monogamous breeding pairs while preying on lemmings and seabirds — what animal is it?
Arctic fox: Species of fox. It is well adapted to living in cold environments, and is known for its thick, warm fur that can be used as camouflage against snow in the winter.
This British mathematician and logician coined the phrase 'mathematical induction' and gave his name to a pair of laws relating conjunction, disjunction, and negation. Who was he?
Augustus De Morgan: British mathematician and logician (1806–1871)

This relationship, expressed as A = εcl, links how much light a solution absorbs directly to its concentration — what is this principle called, named after two scientists whose work dates back to the mid-18th century?
Beer–Lambert law: Scientific law describing absorption of light.
This small Old World flycatcher breeds in rocky habitats from the British Isles to Morocco and central China, staying put in milder areas but migrating from colder ones — what bird is it?
Black redstart: Species of bird. The black redstart (Phoenicurus ochruros) is a small passerine bird in the Old World flycatcher family.
Named for its unusually long forelimbs — Greek for 'arm lizard' — this Late Jurassic sauropod was first described in 1903 from fossils found in Colorado — which dinosaur?
Brachiosaurus: Sauropod dinosaur genus from the late Jurassic Period.
Alongside HTML and JavaScript, which style sheet language handles the layout, colors, and fonts of a webpage — separating presentation from content?
CSS: Style sheet language. CSS is a cornerstone technology of the World Wide Web, alongside HTML and JavaScript.

Time called her the "literary godmother" to Paris's Lost Generation, and her Black Sun Press printed early Hemingway and Henry Miller — but she also patented the first successful modern bra. Who was she?
Usually arising from damage to the developing brain before birth, this group of childhood movement disorders causes stiff or weak muscles, tremors, and poor coordination — what condition?
Cerebral palsy: Movement disorders that appear in early childhood.
Every animal in this group shares five telltale traits — including a notochord, pharyngeal slits, and a tail that extends past the anus — at some stage of life; which of these belongs to that phylum?
Chordate: Phylum of animals having a dorsal nerve cord.
This genus of demersal fish, named by Linnaeus in 1758, includes an Atlantic and a Pacific species prized for their mild flavor and flaky white flesh — what fish is it?
Cod: Common name for several fish, but mainly the demersal genus Gadus.
Caused by a fungus that forms galls on maize plants, this disease produces an edible delicacy in Mexico known as huitlacoche, often stuffed into quesadillas — which condition?
Corn smut: Fungal plant disease on maize and teosinte.
Also called Bermuda grass, this hardy warm-climate turf species is ironically not native to the island of the same name — which plant, by its scientific name?
Cynodon dactylon: Species of grass. Cynodon dactylon, commonly known as Bermuda grass or as couch grass in Australia and New Zealand, is a grass found worldwide in warm and tropical climates.

Found in many cough and cold medicines, this morphinan-class compound was approved by the FDA in 2022 as part of a rapid-acting antidepressant combo, but can act as a dissociative hallucinogen at high doses. What substance is it?
Dextromethorphan: Cough suppressant and dissociative drug.

With nearly 24,000 ommatidia in each compound eye and wings usually held flat rather than folded, this iridescent flying insect is often confused with its lighter-bodied damselfly cousins — what is it?
Named for the large trunk-like proboscis of its males, this giant oceangoing pinniped can weigh up to 4,000 kilograms and was once hunted nearly to extinction for lamp oil. What animal is it?
Elephant seal: Genus of aquatic carnivores.
Sold under the brand name Nexium, this proton pump inhibitor treats acid reflux by blocking an enzyme in the stomach's acid-producing cells — what is it?
Esomeprazole: Medication which reduces stomach acid.
While its deciduous neighbors drop everything and go bare for winter, this kind of plant keeps its foliage green and working all year round — what's the botanical term?
Evergreen: Plant that has leaves in all seasons.

Modern phylogenetics calls this a paraphyletic group covering nearly every vertebrate except the tetrapods — gill-bearing, limbless-of-digits, and usually cold-blooded. What aquatic animals are these?
This mathematical principle links differentiation and integration, showing the two operations to be essentially inverses of each other — what is it called?
Fundamental theorem of calculus: Relationship between derivatives and integrals.
The longest member of the weasel family at up to 1.8 meters, this noisy, highly social river-dweller lives in family groups along the Amazon and in the Pantanal — which animal?
Known as the black shag in New Zealand, this widespread seabird breeds across much of the Old World, Australasia, and the Atlantic coast of North America — which bird?
This German-American physicist won a 1967 Nobel Prize for explaining how a nuclear cycle powers heavy stars, after heading the Theoretical Division at Los Alamos during World War II — who is he?
Also nicknamed 'rose mallow,' this genus of large, showy tropical flowers includes both herbaceous plants and woody shrubs — which genus is it?
Hibiscus: Genus of plants. Hibiscus is a genus of common flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae.
In its pure form it's a faintly blue, syrupy liquid, but the concentrated 'high-test' version decomposes explosively when heated and has even been used as rocket fuel — what compound is it?
Hydrogen peroxide: Chemical compound. The molecule hydrogen peroxide is asymmetrical and highly polarized.
Patented in 1961 and used to fight fever, pain and inflammation by blocking the cyclooxygenase enzyme, this drug sits on the WHO's List of Essential Medicines — what is it?

His 1962 book The Calculus of Consent launched a theory of how politicians' and bureaucrats' self-interest shapes their decisions, earning him the 1986 Nobel in economics — which founder of public choice theory is this?
James M. Buchanan: American economist and Nobel Laureate (1919–2013)
Dubbed the 'Angel of Death,' this German physician held doctorates in both anthropology and medicine before joining the SS and selecting Auschwitz prisoners for the gas chambers — who was he?
Josef Mengele: Nazi SS doctor at Auschwitz (1911–1979)
Bred for their dazzling colors since the early 19th century in Niigata, Japan, these ornamental carp come in patterns like Kōhaku and Shōwa Sanshoku — what are they?
Koi: Colored varieties of Amur carp.
Distinguished by coloured scales, large triangular wings, and a nectar-sipping proboscis, which insect order encompasses both butterflies and moths?
Lepidoptera: Order of insects including moths and butterflies.
Born as a Skunk Works black project and nicknamed "Habu," this Mach 3+ reconnaissance aircraft carried a crew of two in tandem cockpits — which plane is it?
Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird: US Air Force supersonic aircraft, 1964–1998.
First named in 1703 to honor a French botanist, this genus of 200-plus flowering trees and shrubs produces large fragrant blooms and cone-like autumn fruits — which genus?
Magnolia: Genus of angiosperms. Magnolia is a large genus of about 210 to 340 flowering plant species in the subfamily Magnolioideae of the family Magnoliaceae.
This German physicist won the 1914 Nobel for discovering how crystals diffract X-rays, then — a fierce opponent of Nazism — helped rebuild German science after the war. Who is he?
This colorless gas, made by swapping one hydrogen atom in ammonia for a methyl group, has a strong rotten-fish smell and serves as a building block for many compounds — what is it?
Sold under the brand name Provigil, this first-line narcolepsy treatment boosts dopamine without the euphoria or addiction risk of classic stimulants like amphetamine — what is it?
This autoimmune disease attacks acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, often causing drooping eyelids, double vision, and difficulty swallowing — which condition?
Myasthenia gravis: Autoimmune disease resulting in skeletal muscle weakness.
This semiaquatic salamander's juvenile phase is nicknamed an 'eft,' and adults return to the water every year to breed after living mostly on land — what is it?
Newt: Salamander in the subfamily Pleurodelinae.

This family within the superfamily Delphinoidea includes species with 'whale' in their common names, like the pilot and false killer types, and ranges up in size to the massive orca — what is this family called?
Oceanic dolphin: Family of marine mammals.

Triggered by a surge of luteinizing hormone near the midpoint of the menstrual cycle, this event sees the ovarian follicle rupture and release an egg — which breaks down in under a day if it isn't fertilized. What is it called?
Ovulation: Release of egg cells from the ovaries.
This Stanford biologist became famous — and controversial — for his 1968 book warning that runaway population growth would bring famine and resource depletion. Who was he?
This inherited metabolic disorder, caused by mutations in the PAH gene, leaves patients unable to break down a certain amino acid and can give off a musty odor if untreated — what is it?
Phenylketonuria: Amino acid metabolic disorder. Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an inborn error of metabolism that results in decreased metabolism of the amino acid phenylalanine.
Caused by viral infections, autoimmune disorders, or pulmonary embolism, this condition inflames the membranes lining the lungs and chest cavity, causing sharp pain when breathing — which condition?
Pleurisy: Disease of the lungs. Pleurisy, also known as pleuritis, is inflammation of the membranes that surround the lungs and line the chest cavity (pleurae).
First prescribed in 1934, this steroid sex hormone plays a key role in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryonic development — what is it?
Progesterone: Sex hormone. Progesterone (P4) is an endogenous steroid and progestogen sex hormone involved in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryogenesis of humans and other species.
This is the name for three positive whole numbers a, b, and c satisfying a² + b² = c², like the classic set (3, 4, 5) — what is it called?
Pythagorean triple: Integer side lengths of a right triangle.
Spanning turtles, crocodilians, the lizards-and-snakes of Squamata, and the lone tuatara, which group of ectothermic, amniotic animals does herpetology study?
Reptile: Class of animals. The study of the traditional reptile orders, customarily in combination with the study of modern amphibians, is called herpetology.
Native to tropical Africa and the Indian subcontinent, this medium-sized parrot has established wild populations worldwide after pet-trade escapees adapted brilliantly to city life — which bird?

Rose-ringed parakeet: Species of bird. The rose-ringed parakeet (Psittacula krameri), also known as the ring-necked parakeet, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula, of the family Psittaculidae.
This Sapporo-born programmer rose to become Nintendo's fourth president, betting on novel, entertaining games over the most powerful hardware — who is he?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Satoru Iwata: Japanese video game executive (1959–2015)
In this biological process, haploid gametes such as sperm and egg cells combine to form a zygote that develops into a diploid organism — what is it called?
Sexual reproduction: Biological process. Sexual reproduction is the most common life cycle in multicellular eukaryotes, such as animals, fungi and plants.
Known as caustic soda or lye, this white ionic solid is so corrosive it breaks down fats and proteins at room temperature and eagerly drinks moisture from the air — what compound is it?
Sodium hydroxide: Caustic soda, with formula NaOH.
The most extreme form of malnutrition — a calorie deficit too deep to sustain life, sometimes wielded as a weapon and a crime under international law — goes by what name?
Starvation: Caloric intake below what is needed to maintain an organism's life.
This South African biologist made a tiny roundworm, C. elegans, the model organism for studying how bodies develop, sharing a 2002 Nobel for the work — who is he?
Sydney Brenner: South African biologist and Nobel prize winner (1927–2019)

Believing he'd been commanded to build the biblical Third Temple, this engineer single-handedly created an operating system written in a language he invented himself, despite later struggles with schizophrenia and homelessness — who was he?
Terry A. Davis: American computer programmer (1969–2018)
With the symbol Sn and atomic number 50, this metal emits a crackling 'cry' when bent and boasts more stable isotopes than any other element — which one?
Tin: Chemical element with atomic number 50 (Sn). A metallic-gray metal, tin is soft enough to be cut with little force, and a bar of tin can be bent by hand with little effort.
Nicknamed 'rabbit fever' and spread by ticks, deer flies or contact with infected animals, this bacterial infection causes fever, skin ulcers and swollen lymph nodes — what is it?
Tularemia: Infectious disease caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis.
Found only in the northern Gulf of California, this porpoise is the smallest living cetacean and is critically endangered due to bycatch from an illegal fishery — which species?
Vaquita: Endangered species of porpoise. The vaquita ( və-KEE-tə; Phocoena sinus) is a species of porpoise endemic to the northern end of the Gulf of California in Baja California, Mexico.

Also known as 'wet brain,' this neurological condition results from a severe thiamine deficiency and classically presents with confusion, poor coordination, and eye movement problems — which condition is it?
Wernicke encephalopathy: Medical condition. The condition is part of a larger group of thiamine deficiency disorders that includes beriberi, in all its forms, and alcoholic Korsakoff syndrome.
This Egyptian archaeologist twice served as his country's Minister of Tourism and Antiquities and has dug at sites from the Nile Delta to the Western Desert — who is he?
What is the chemical symbol for bromine?
The symbol for bromine is Br. Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.
Tantalum is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for tantalum is Ta. Tantalum is a chemical element; it has symbol Ta and atomic number 73.

Jane Fonda: Jane Seymour Fonda (born December 21, 1937) is an American actress and activist.

Richard Gere: Richard Tiffany Gere ( GHEER; born August 31, 1949) is an American actor.

Drew Barrymore: Drew Blythe Barrymore (born February 22, 1975) is an American actress, producer, talk show host, and businesswoman.

Richard Harris: Richard St John Francis Harris (1 October 1930 – 25 October 2002) was an Irish actor and singer.
